Stage 2 returns to object-position and updated-digit information. Questions differ only in recipient: 𗘈 versus agent_0 or agent_7, supporting “everyone.” Lists of named recipients place 𗄼 between them, supporting “and.” Report and question envelopes recur with both 𗪩…𗼛 and 𗥐…𗃚, while 𘚜 alternates with 𗟆 in the corresponding relation slot. This establishes syntax more securely than any guessed object name.

The number mapping is not taken solely from task feedback. Message3 places X at position𘁁 and message2 assigns it digit𗶞. Message8 places W at position𗶞 and messages15/22 assign W digit𗬵. The accepted ordered code begins 𗶞,𗬵. Thus interpreting the clues as positions and digits gives 𘁁=1 and 𗶞=2. Stage expressions in messages36/43 and76 independently align with public stages1 and2. 1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

This is a partial reconstruction, not a claim to recover the original file verbatim. Confidence labels concern meanings, not merely the existence of repeated patterns. Untranslated glyphs are deliberately retained.

GRAMMAR AND MESSAGE CONVENTIONS
• [High] Messages commonly have the form ACT 𗪩 agent_N 𗼛 BODY. The literal agent identifier names the speaker. A parallel form is ACT 𗥐 agent_N 𗃚 BODY, often used for a second clause in the same message.
• [High] 𘊌 introduces a report/assertion. [High] 𗀉 introduces a question/request for information. [Medium-high] 𗱓 introduces a submission, proposed action, or attempted command.
• [Medium] 𘒳 introduces a further report/action clause; its precise distinction from 𘊌 is unknown. [Low] 𘆣 is another follow-on speech act, possibly a further request. [Low] 𗏶 and 𘚑 are additional speech-act markers, exact meanings unknown.
• [High] 𘚜 separates a topic/property from its value, or a requested topic from its recipient. Thus it is not necessarily an arithmetic equals sign. [Medium-high] 𗟆 performs the parallel function with the alternate envelope.
• [High] 𗄼 joins list members, approximately “and.” [Medium-high] 𗘈 means “everyone/all,” particularly as the recipient of questions. [High] 𗑸 marks the end of a question/request.
• [Medium] 𘚐 is an assertion-ending or epistemic particle; 𘚄 and 𘌔 are alternative endings. Their exact distinctions are unknown. They may encode certainty/evidence rather than punctuation. They are not treated here as digits. [Medium] 𗋭 is associated with submissions/imperatives.
• [Medium] Some messages omit the usual separator or ending. Multiple complete clauses can occur in one chat message. Word order varies somewhat: a key/object description can precede or follow 𘚺.

NUMBERS
• [High] 𘁁 = 1; 𗶞 = 2. This is supported jointly by position clues, the submitted code, and stage labels.
• [Medium-high] 𘇩 = 3; 𗾌 = 4. These fill the remaining positions in a four-position puzzle, and recur consistently in the next stage.
• [Medium] 𗬵 and 𗒏 are numeric/digit-like values in the first code, but their actual numerical values are not recovered. 𗊓 and 𗈵 also occur in value-like contexts, but are unmapped. [Low] 𗡒 may be a value, answer token, or something else; unknown.

TASK VOCABULARY
• [Medium-high] 𘝞 = stage. [Low-medium] 𗿋 = now/current, as in “stage 2 now.”
• [Medium] 𗜀 = code/answer. 𗡕 = position/index. 𘏛 is a modifier in the initial position/code expressions; exact meaning unknown. It could distinguish initial/code positions.
• [Medium] 𗇽 = new/final, especially before position or key. 𘚺 = key/object, or the relation identifying a key/object.
• [Medium] 𗹕 = digit/value. 𗅲 modifies the original/code digit expression; exact gloss unknown. 𗁳 means new/current in updated-value expressions. [Low-medium] 𘆎 is another element of the updated-value expression 𘆎 𗁳.
• [Medium] 𗤄 = clue/information. [Low] 𗭵 may mean private/own in requests for an agent's clue.
• [Medium] 𘅌 = press/activate, or an action command on an item. 𗾨 = done/pressed/accepted. [Low] 𗨞 is another action-status/prerequisite term, possibly not-yet or required.
• [Low-medium] 𘍂 names an ordering/prerequisite property. [Low] 𗌩 names a separate button property, possibly a numeric effect, label, or rank.
• [Low] 𗣎 is unresolved. It occurs in a changing digit/state expression 𗣎 𗹕, in 𗅲 𗣎 𗹕, and before 2 in a button property. Possibilities include current/last, a counter/state term, or a negative/minus operator. These are alternatives, not recovered meanings.
• [Low] 𗘺, 𘆄, 𗪐, 𘋍 name four actionable items. Their real labels, perhaps button colors, are not recovered. Below they are called A, B, C, D respectively. [Medium-high] The successful action sequence was A→B→C→D.
• [Low] Recurring object descriptions include 𘅪 (X), 𗷤 𗉞 (Y), 𘋉 𗜘 (Z), 𗎶 𘍧 (W), 𗍽 𗊓 (V), and 𗍽 𘍧 (V′). These labels are placeholders, not translations. Shared glyphs suggest compositional descriptions, possibly color/shape or other properties, rather than necessarily indivisible names. W's relationship to lone 𗎶 and to 𗛽 is unresolved; V and V′ must not silently be equated.
• [Low] 𗪤, 𘋉/𗜘 individually, 𗪐/𘋍 individually, 𗁳 outside the above compounds, 𗳵, 𗲅, 𘙠, 𘆮, 𗡑, 𗸽, 𘉝, 𗄪, and 𗊑 have no securely recovered independent gloss. Some are covered only through compound/contextual interpretations above.

Quoted unknown glyphs remain untranslated. Common ending particles are omitted from readable English unless relevant; their unresolved status is recorded above. A secondary clause introduced by 𘒳 is marked “Further clause,” without assuming its exact speech act.

3. THE TASK

[Medium-high confidence] The agents were solving a cooperative, staged puzzle using distributed clues. There were at least three active stages, publicly numbered 0, 1, and 2; reaching stage 3 apparently ended or advanced beyond the displayed puzzle. The evaluator counted invalid attempts.

Stage 0 appears to ask for a four-symbol/numeral code derived by combining object-position clues with object-digit clues. The agents requested missing information from everyone or particular agents. The first accepted submission, message 19, was the four tokens 𗶞 𗬵 𘇩 𗒏, approximately 2, unknown, 3, unknown. Their actual second and fourth decimal values are not recovered. Repetitions after the transition to stage 1 were rejected. The initial clues are not completely reconciled: V and V′ differ, and Z's position and V's digit cannot safely be assigned to the same object without an additional assumption.

Stage 1 appears to involve four buttons/actions and prerequisite or numeric-effect clues. The eventual successful sequence was A=𗘺, B=𘆄, C=𗪐, D=𘋍. It may also involve a changing counter/digit or target, since 𗣎-related values vary. Agent_6 apparently executed the useful progression: message 49 begins with press A; message 55 reports A done and presses B; message 64 reports B done and presses C; message 68 reports C done and presses D, after which stage 2 is announced. Other agents attempted duplicate presses, complete-sequence formats, or stale code submissions, producing invalid counts. This suggests successful intermediate presses need not generate public feedback; silence is not evidence that nothing happened. Whether agent identity itself mattered is unknown.

Stage 2 returns to object-position and updated-digit information. Conditional on the inferred vocabulary and numerals, the clues imply a likely final code 1,4,3,2: new position1 is Y and Y's new digit is1; new position2 is V and V's new digit is4; new position4 is W and W's updated digit is2; the remaining X has updated digit3 and presumably occupies position3. This last placement is inference by elimination, not an explicit translated report. Many agents kept asking for positions3/4, and some continued stale stage1 actions, increasing invalid attempts to16. The record does not contain a securely decoded explicit submission of 1432. Message95 is unresolved, and message97 merely establishes that the public state reached stage3 with16 invalid attempts. We cannot identify the final trigger with confidence.

4. EVIDENCE

The strongest evidence is substitution within repeated grammatical slots. Questions differ only in recipient: 𗘈 versus agent_0 or agent_7, supporting “everyone.” Lists of named recipients place 𗄼 between them, supporting “and.” Report and question envelopes recur with both 𗪩…𗼛 and 𗥐…𗃚, while 𘚜 alternates with 𗟆 in the corresponding relation slot. This establishes syntax more securely than any guessed object name.

The number mapping is not taken solely from task feedback. Message3 places X at position𘁁 and message2 assigns it digit𗶞. Message8 places W at position𗶞 and messages15/22 assign W digit𗬵. The accepted ordered code begins 𗶞,𗬵. Thus interpreting the clues as positions and digits gives 𘁁=1 and 𗶞=2. Stage expressions in messages36/43 and76 independently align with public stages1 and2. The remaining position symbols𘇩 and𗾌 plausibly mean3 and4, but with less independent anchoring: differently written entity descriptions would need to be equivalent to connect all the initial clues. No equivalent anchor identifies 𗬵 or𗒏's decimal values.

Action semantics rely on both language and behavior: message55 says A𗾨 followed by B𘅌; message64 says B𗾨 followed by C𘅌; message68 says C𗾨 followed by D𘅌 and the stage advances. This supports completed/pressed versus press/activate, and the sequence A–B–C–D. It does not prove exact color names or all command grammar. The evaluator also reacts to some messages headed as reports, so speech-act labels alone do not define what the external parser executes.

Updated-position/value interpretations are supported by the parallel stage0 and stage2 clause structures and by separate agents contributing complementary constraints. However, the actual object descriptions are not grounded to English colors/shapes. Shared components in 𗍽𗊓, 𗍽𘍧 and 𗎶𘍧, and the unusual W-code clause in95, argue against presenting opaque object labels as confidently decoded nouns.

Although the latter alone could suggest −2, a simple minus-sign reading does not explain both constructions and remains weak. 𗣎𗹕 could be a counter/state or signed value rather than “last digit.” 𘚐/𘚄/𘌔 may express confidence or evidential source, not sentence type; 𗹫 is another unresolved ending. The original file or independently grounded usages showing these distinctions would change those interpretations. Evidence that position symbols are not ordinary ordered indices, or that successful actions are parsed by different rules, would weaken the numerical and stage1 deductions.
